draft.title: Making a personal budget
card: A budget is a plan that lists the money you expect to receive (income) and the money you expect to spend (expenses) over a period, such as a month.
expenses that stay the same each time, such as a phone plan or a gym fee.
expenses that can go up or down, such as snacks, clothes or bus fares.
Subtract total expenses from income to see what is left to save. If expenses are higher than income, the budget shows a shortfall, and you need to cut costs or earn more.
draft.remember: Income minus expenses shows what is left to save.

a.q: Which of these would be a fixed cost in a budget?
opts: A phone plan that costs $30 every month
Movie tickets bought on some weekends
Lunch from the canteen on different days
A new jumper bought when it gets cold
a.why: A phone plan costs the same amount each month, so it is a fixed cost. The other items change from month to month depending on what the person chooses to buy.
a.clue: Which cost is the same every time?

b.q: Jaden earns $200 a month from a weekend job. His fixed costs are $60 and his changing costs are $150. What does his budget show?
opts: A shortfall of $10, so he must cut costs
$140 left over, so he can save that amount
A shortfall of $60, because fixed costs are too high
$50 left over, because changing costs are not counted
b.why: Total expenses are $60 + $150 = $210, which is more than his income of $200. The budget shows a shortfall of $10. Changing costs must be counted, so the answer of $50 left over is wrong.
b.clue: Add both kinds of cost before subtracting from income.

a.best: A phone plan that costs $30 every month

b.best: A shortfall of $10, so he must cut costs

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a precise amount and 'every month', which echoes the clue 'the same every time'. A student could pick it without knowing what a fixed cost is.
The right option says he 'must cut costs', but the card says you need to cut costs or earn more. The option is too absolute and leaves out earning more.

The distractor '$50 left over, because changing costs are not counted' does not add up: $200 − $150 = $50 leaves out the fixed costs, not the changing costs. The why repeats this mismatch, which could confuse students.

check.summary: Both answers are correct, but in question a the right option gives itself away with its precise detail, and in question b the right option says 'must cut costs' when the card also allows earning more. One distractor in b also has reasoning that does not match its own number.

proposal.title: Making a personal budget
card: A budget is a plan that lists the money you expect to receive (income) and the money you expect to spend (expenses) over a period, such as a month.
expenses that stay the same each time, such as a phone plan or a gym fee.
expenses that can go up or down, such as snacks, clothes or bus fares.
Subtract total expenses from income to see what is left to save. If expenses are higher than income, the budget shows a shortfall, and you need to cut costs or earn more.
proposal.remember: Income minus all expenses, fixed and changing, shows what is left to save.

a.q: Mia lists what she spent on four things in March and April. Which is a fixed cost?
opts: Music app: $12 in March, $12 in April
Snacks: $18 in March, $25 in April
Bus fares: $30 in March, $22 in April
Clothes: $0 in March, $45 in April
a.why: The music app cost the same amount in both months, so it is a fixed cost. Snacks, bus fares and clothes went up or down between months, so they are changing costs, even though bus fares are paid often.
a.clue: Compare the two months for each item.

b.q: Jaden earns $200 a month from a weekend job. His fixed costs are $60 and his changing costs are $150. What does his budget show?
opts: A shortfall of $10, so he needs to cut costs or earn more
$10 left over, so he can save $10 a month from his job
$140 left over, because only fixed costs are counted
$50 left over, because only changing costs are counted
b.why: Total expenses are $60 + $150 = $210, which is $10 more than his income of $200, so the budget shows a shortfall. The $140 and $50 answers each subtract only one kind of cost, but a budget counts both fixed and changing costs.
b.clue: Add both kinds of cost before comparing with income.

b.best: A shortfall of $10, so he needs to cut costs or earn more
